beats.label: S1 · Bone in the Hills
beats.text: Bosch shoots a suspect and faces a wrongful death suit. A dog finds a child's bone reopening a 1989 cold case that dredges up his own childhood abuse.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes Bosch's professional stakes and the cold case that anchors the season.

beats.label: S1 · Waits Surrenders
beats.text: Van driver Raynard Waits confesses to the child's murder to avoid the death penalty. Pedophile suspect Nicholas Trent hangs himself as investigators close in.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Waits, the season's engine, and eliminates the misdirection suspect.

beats.label: S1 · The Field Trip
beats.text: On a field trip to victim sites, DA O'Shea forces Bosch to uncuff Waits, who shoots the Deputy DA and escapes. O'Shea publicly blames Bosch.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The escape and public blame set the O'Shea vs Bosch dynamic that continues into S2.

beats.label: S1 · Orphanage Ties
beats.text: Bosch identifies the boy as Arthur Delacroix and traces Waits back through their shared orphanage. Waits hides with his oblivious mother, then murders her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Positions Bosch as the one who understands Waits and makes the personal pursuit possible.

beats.label: S1 · Suicide by Cop
beats.text: Using Eleanor's FBI profiling, Bosch corners Waits during a hostage rescue and kills him. Irving reveals Waits's gun was unloaded — 'suicide by cop.'
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes the Waits threat but reinforces Bosch's willingness to use lethal force when cornered.

beats.label: S1 · Stokes Walks
beats.text: The real Delacroix killer is juvenile Johnny Stokes, who walks free; a grieving Sam Delacroix then murders Stokes in vengeance.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Delivers the season's ironic solution and shows justice landing outside the law.

beats.label: S1 · Badge on the Desk
beats.text: After Captain Pounds threatens him, Bosch shoves him through a window and hands his gun and badge to Billets, hoping to reach Maddie.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends the season with Bosch off the job — the state S2 has to walk back from.

cliffhanger.text: Bosch has handed in his badge to Billets after assaulting a superior officer. The real Delacroix killer is dead by Sam's hand — and Bosch's career and any real chance of time with Maddie hang unresolved.
questions: Will Bosch face criminal charges for shoving Pounds through the window?
Does he even want the badge back now that the Delacroix case is closed?
Will his push to be with Maddie in Vegas actually happen?

characters.name: Harry Bosch
characters.line: LAPD homicide detective who just handed in his badge after shoving Captain Pounds through a window; the Delacroix case has left him wanting time with his daughter.

characters.name: Jerry Edgar
characters.line: Bosch's steadier, more procedural partner; worked the Waits and Delacroix cases with him from the start.

characters.name: Deputy Chief Irving
characters.line: Politically astute LAPD leader who backed Bosch through the Waits fallout despite their frequent clashes.

characters.name: Lt. Grace Billets
characters.line: Bosch's direct supervisor; accepted his badge at season's end but sympathetic to his methods.

characters.name: Eleanor Wish
characters.line: Bosch's ex-wife in Las Vegas and former FBI profiler; helped him profile Waits and remains mother of his teenage daughter.

characters.name: Madeline 'Maddie' Bosch
characters.line: Harry's teenage daughter; lives with Eleanor but ran away to LA mid-season seeking her father.

characters.name: Raynard Waits
characters.line: Van-driving serial killer who confessed to Delacroix, escaped custody by killing the Deputy DA, and was ultimately shot dead by Bosch.

beats.label: S2 · Trunk Music
beats.text: The trunk-murder body of pornographer Tony Allen ties Bosch's case to Vegas gangster Joey Marks. Irving's son George goes undercover for IA in narcotics.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the season's two engines — the Allen investigation and George's parallel undercover work.

beats.label: S2 · Vegas Poker
beats.text: Bosch travels to Vegas and finds Eleanor played poker with Allen days before his death; LVPD leverages the tie into a joint investigation.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Pulls Eleanor into the case and keeps her present in Bosch's life through the season.

beats.label: S2 · George Exposed
beats.text: Allen's security head Carl Nash exposes George as an IA mole and has him assassinated, devastating Chief Irving.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The event that pushes Irving into accepting the Chief role and personally investing in this case.

beats.label: S2 · Veronica's Play
beats.text: Bosch learns Rykov is undercover FBI (Luke Goshen) and deduces Veronica Allen hired Nash to kill her husband for the money.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reveals the true conspiracy and sets up the S3 mistrial fallout with O'Shea.

beats.label: S2 · Interim Chief
beats.text: Irving accepts an interim Chief promotion in exchange for a fair probe into his son's death. Nash flees a bank shootout that kills Marks.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Elevates Irving to Chief — the position that defines his arc from here on.

beats.label: S2 · Nash's Grenade
beats.text: Nash is killed by his own grenade during his capture; Veronica walks free after murdering the priest hiding Layla.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes the case mechanically but leaves Veronica's walk as the season's unfinished business.

beats.label: S2 · Fox Mitchell
beats.text: An old friend leads Bosch to Fox Mitchell as his mother's killer — but Mitchell already died of cancer, robbing Bosch of his justice.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Opens the mother's-murder thread as Bosch's ongoing private hunt across the seasons ahead.

cliffhanger.text: Veronica Allen has walked free for orchestrating her husband's murder. Irving is now interim Chief while grieving his only son, and Bosch's trail to his mother's killer has died with Fox Mitchell.
questions: Will Veronica ever face real justice for what she engineered?
Can Irving hold the department together while carrying his son's death?
Is Fox Mitchell really Bosch's mother's killer, or is Bosch being misled?

characters.name: Harry Bosch
characters.line: LAPD homicide detective; the Allen investigation and his mother's cold case have consumed his year.

characters.name: Jerry Edgar
characters.line: Bosch's partner; helped close the Allen and Nash case with him.

characters.name: Chief Irving
characters.line: Just accepted interim Chief after DA O'Shea forced through his son George's murder investigation; grieving and estranged from Connie.

characters.name: Lt. Grace Billets
characters.line: Bosch's supervisor in Hollywood Division.

characters.name: Eleanor Wish
characters.line: Bosch's ex-wife; still in Vegas with Maddie, briefly kidnapped by Nash's crew and rescued.

characters.name: Madeline 'Maddie' Bosch
characters.line: Harry's daughter; taken hostage alongside Eleanor during the case.

characters.name: Veronica Allen
characters.line: Tony Allen's widow who conspired with Carl Nash to kill her husband; walked free after framing Nash for the murder.

characters.name: Carl Nash
characters.line: Allen's security head and Veronica's lover; masterminded the trunk murder and George Irving's assassination; killed by his own grenade during capture.

beats.label: S3 · Gunn in the Crosshairs
beats.text: Bosch secretly begins building a case against freed killer Ed Gunn. Veronica Allen's trial ends in mistrial; Bosch publicly berates DA O'Shea for tanking it.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the parallel Gunn-vendetta thread and the O'Shea grudge from S2 fallout.

beats.label: S3 · Meadows and Gunn
beats.text: Homeless vet Billy Meadows is murdered; Ed Gunn is found dead soon after. Billets quietly orders Edgar to investigate Bosch as Gunn's killer.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kicks off the season's main case and the Edgar-investigating-Bosch friction.

beats.label: S3 · Dobbs's Crew
beats.text: Bosch traces Meadows to army buddy Trevor Dobbs and his crew smuggling Middle East cash. Witness Sharkey is murdered after Bosch questions him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the season's real antagonists and shows the moral cost of Bosch's methods.

beats.label: S3 · Holland's Frame
beats.text: Andrew Holland's team frames Bosch for Gunn's murder through a press campaign. Detective Caffrey, lead on Bosch's mother's case, dies in a targeted arson.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Caffrey's death is the bridge that will eventually reveal Bradley Walker.

beats.label: S3 · The Leaked Tape
beats.text: Bosch leaks doctored footage of Jessie Tafero at Gunn's scene; Rudy Tafero flips on Andrew Holland, who is arrested for Gunn's murder.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The moral inflection that will crack Bosch's partnership with Edgar.

beats.label: S3 · Island Capture
beats.text: Edgar kills Woody; Xavi retaliates by shooting Edgar, then dies at Dobbs's hand. Bosch pursues Dobbs to an island and captures him after a shootout.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes the Meadows conspiracy and leaves Edgar wounded in the trust between them.

beats.label: S3 · Walker Named
beats.text: Edgar realizes Bosch leaked the tape. Eleanor returns from Vegas as an FBI asset. Bosch learns his mother's real killer is Bradley Walker, police commission president.
beats.whyLoadBearing: All three of S4's launching threads: Edgar's discovery, Eleanor's return, Walker's exposure.

cliffhanger.text: Bosch now knows the man who killed his mother is the sitting president of the police commission. Eleanor has quietly returned to LA as an FBI asset, and Edgar has realized Bosch bent the rules to close the Holland case.
questions: How does Bosch bring down a killer as untouchable as Bradley Walker?
What does Eleanor's FBI work have her doing so close to home?
Can the Bosch-Edgar partnership survive the tape-leak betrayal?

characters.name: Harry Bosch
characters.line: LAPD homicide detective; framed and cleared this season, and now knows the man who killed his mother.

characters.name: Jerry Edgar
characters.line: Bosch's partner; shot and wounded by Xavi; realized only at season's end that Bosch anonymously leaked the tape.

characters.name: Chief Irving
characters.line: LAPD Chief; began a new personal chapter this season alongside his political rise.

characters.name: Lt. Grace Billets
characters.line: Hollywood Division lieutenant; briefly ordered Edgar to investigate Bosch as a suspect.

characters.name: Eleanor Wish
characters.line: Bosch's ex-wife; just returned from Vegas and revealed to be working for the FBI in Los Angeles.

characters.name: Madeline 'Maddie' Bosch
characters.line: Harry's daughter; living in LA now closer to both parents.

characters.name: Bradley Walker
characters.line: President of the police commission and Bosch's newly identified target — the man who killed his mother years ago.

beats.label: S4 · Angel's Flight
beats.text: Attorney Howard Elias is shot dead on Angel's Flight the night before his Black Guardian police brutality trial. Irving puts Bosch on the task force.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the political weight of the Elias case and Bosch's central task force role.

beats.label: S4 · Sheehan Flees
beats.text: Detective Frank Sheehan flees when ballistics tie his gun to Elias; he becomes the prime suspect after a drunken confession of Black Guardian abuse to Bosch.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sheehan is the misdirection that anchors the first half of the season.

beats.label: S4 · Eleanor Killed
beats.text: Eleanor is shot dead by hitmen tied to a Chinese national she'd secretly photographed at a poker game. A grieving Maddie moves in with Bosch.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The emotional pivot of the whole show; Maddie now lives with Bosch full-time from here.

beats.label: S4 · Framed
beats.text: Bosch talks Sheehan into surrendering and confirms he was framed. He finds hidden camera footage of Sheehan and Terry Drake torturing the Black Guardian victim.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Clears Sheehan of murder and confirms the Black Guardian corruption Elias was trying to expose.

beats.label: S4 · Karaoke Shootout
beats.text: Hunting Eleanor's killers, Bosch's team kills one at a karaoke bar; the escapee is later found dead with Bosch's business card in his mouth.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Bosch's personal hunt for Eleanor's killers runs alongside the Elias case.

beats.label: S4 · Lincoln Confesses
beats.text: Detective Lincoln confesses she and Walker fed evidence to Elias for cash; Elias's decision to publicly try Black Guardian would have exposed Walker as the source.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Makes Walker viable as the true Elias killer and links back to the S3 revelation.

beats.label: S4 · Walker Confesses
beats.text: Bosch finds Walker's secret Biltmore passage to Angel's Flight and pressures him into confessing both Elias's murder and his mother's. Bosch and Maddie spread Eleanor's ashes.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes the mother's-murder arc from S2 and S3 and leaves Bosch as Maddie's sole parent.

cliffhanger.text: Bosch has finally forced Walker to confess to both Elias's murder and his mother's, and buried Eleanor with Maddie in the desert. He's raising her alone now, still uneasy with Edgar and unsure who else in the department was helping Walker.
questions: How does Bosch raise a grieving teenage Maddie on his own?
Did FBI Agent Griffin knowingly compromise Eleanor to the Chinese?
Are there other Walker collaborators still buried inside the LAPD?

characters.name: Harry Bosch
characters.line: LAPD homicide detective; caught his mother's killer at last but lost Eleanor along the way.

characters.name: Jerry Edgar
characters.line: Bosch's partner; the friction from Bosch's S3 tape leak still shadows their work.

characters.name: Chief Irving
characters.line: LAPD Chief; oversaw the Elias task force and continues as Bosch's political cover.

characters.name: Lt. Grace Billets
characters.line: Bosch's supervisor in Hollywood Division.

characters.name: Madeline 'Maddie' Bosch
characters.line: Harry's teenage daughter; moved in with him full-time after Eleanor was murdered.

characters.name: Frank Sheehan
characters.line: RHD detective framed for the Elias killing; cleared of that murder but confessed to Bosch he participated in the Black Guardian torture.

characters.name: Bradley Walker
characters.line: Former police commission president; just confessed to killing both Howard Elias and Bosch's mother, now under arrest.

beats.label: S5 · Pharmacy and Appeal
beats.text: Bosch investigates a pharmacy murder while his 1996 conviction of Preston Borders is appealed by ex-girlfriend prosecutor Christina Henry on new DNA evidence.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the two parallel threats — the pill-mill case and the personal Borders appeal.

beats.label: S5 · Elizabeth and Daisy
beats.text: Bosch meets fellow addict Elizabeth Clayton at a VA group; her daughter Daisy's murder remains unsolved. He becomes personally invested.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Opens the Daisy cold case that will anchor the emotional plotline of S6.

beats.label: S5 · Undercover Clinic
beats.text: Undercover as an addict, Bosch infiltrates Dr. Garcia's clinic and links it to a nationwide opioid trafficking operation run by Walsh.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The undercover work sets up the season's climactic desert compound raid.

beats.label: S5 · Edgar's Investigation
beats.text: Edgar investigates his CI Gary Wise's murder, tracing corrupt narcotics detectives Marcos and Arias to Haitian war criminal Jacques Avril.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Edgar's private pursuit of Marcos, Arias, and Avril directly launches the opening of S6.

beats.label: S5 · Russian Roulette
beats.text: Bosch's cover is blown by a leaked news article; he's flown to a desert compound, survives Walsh's Russian roulette, and kills his captors on the return jet.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's most violent turn and the beginning of Walsh's personal war on Bosch.

beats.label: S5 · Irving Buries It
beats.text: Chandler exposes the Borders appeal as a Cronyn frame; the appeal is denied. Bosch discovers Irving destroyed key evidence long ago and confronts him — Irving buries it.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Chandler emerges as an ally, and Irving's evidence tampering becomes leverage Bosch is sitting on.

beats.label: S5 · Home Invasion
beats.text: Walsh and his last men storm Bosch's home; Bosch kills all three. Irving announces his mayoral run; Edgar confronts Marcos and Arias, who threaten him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes Walsh but leaves Irving's political ambition and Edgar's dangerous enemies live going into S6.

cliffhanger.text: Bosch survived a coordinated attempt on his life and dismantled the Borders frame, but he now holds evidence that his own Chief tampered with a case file — and buried it. Edgar has just made lethal enemies inside his own department.
questions: What does Bosch do with what he knows about Irving's evidence tampering?
Can Edgar survive going after Marcos, Arias, and Avril alone?
With Elizabeth still adrift, does the Daisy Clayton case get any further?

characters.name: Harry Bosch
characters.line: LAPD homicide detective; survived Walsh's revenge and cleared his name on the Borders appeal, but now knows Irving committed evidence tampering.

characters.name: Jerry Edgar
characters.line: Bosch's partner; just publicly threatened by Marcos and Arias after exposing their corruption.

characters.name: Chief Irving
characters.line: LAPD Chief; just announced his run for mayor while burying his own coverup of a rushed 1996 arrest.

characters.name: Lt. Grace Billets
characters.line: Hollywood Division lieutenant.

characters.name: Madeline 'Maddie' Bosch
characters.line: Harry's daughter; interned at the DA's office this year and moved out after her breakup with Tom.

characters.name: Honey Chandler
characters.line: Defense attorney who dismantled the Cronyn-Borders conspiracy to frame Bosch; increasingly his ally when their interests align.

characters.name: Elizabeth Clayton
characters.line: Recovering addict Bosch met undercover; her daughter Daisy's unsolved murder is now his next personal case.

characters.name: Marcos & Arias
characters.line: Corrupt narcotics detectives tied to Haitian war criminal Jacques Avril and Gary Wise's murder; Edgar has just made them dangerous enemies.

beats.label: S6 · Cesium Missing
beats.text: Marcos and Arias are killed by their Jamaican targets after Edgar's stakeout is spotted. Physicist Stanley Kent is murdered, 32 vials of cesium missing — terror alert.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Cold-opens with Edgar's S5 pursuit turning fatal and launches the cesium case that drives the season.

beats.label: S6 · Botched Raid
beats.text: The FBI's hunt for the radical 308 group leads to a botched raid; a Strout brother is killed and Officer Powers is crippled.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the 308 as season antagonist and plants the seed of Heather Strout's revenge plot.

beats.label: S6 · No Terror Plot
beats.text: The cesium turns up in a homeless camp — no terror plot. Bosch pivots to widow Alicia Kent, uncovering her affair with FBI Agent Maxwell.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reframes the whole case from terror to domestic murder and points at the real killer.

beats.label: S6 · Daisy Revived
beats.text: Bosch reopens the Daisy Clayton case; Elizabeth leads him to crime scene cleaner Roger Dillon, whose van links to a human trafficking ring.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resolves the cold case seeded in S5 and directly triggers Elizabeth's collapse.

beats.label: S6 · Alicia Flips
beats.text: Alicia flips on Maxwell for a plea; Agent Reece kills Maxwell during pursuit. Alicia is later convicted of conspiracy to murder her husband.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes the Kent case and confirms the season's central plot.

beats.label: S6 · Irving Out
beats.text: A 1996 cassette exposing Irving's chief coverup surfaces; rival Killoran blackmails him out of the mayoral race.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Irving's exit reshapes LA's political landscape as Mayor Lopez inherits his backing into S7.

beats.label: S6 · Avril at Home
beats.text: Elizabeth overdoses after her daughter's killer bargains down. A 308 courtroom bomb is defused. Edgar kills Avril at home — Bosch suspects it wasn't self-defense.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Three season-launching threads for S7: Bosch alone again, bomb plot averted, and Edgar's fragile state.

cliffhanger.text: Bosch has caught the man behind Daisy Clayton but lost Elizabeth to grief. Irving is out of the mayoral race and politically wounded, and Edgar has just killed a man in what Bosch believes was murder, not self-defense.
questions: Was Edgar's shooting of Avril really self-defense, or the calculated act Bosch fears?
Now that Irving is stepping aside, who inherits LA's political future?
Can Bosch and Edgar keep working together with this suspicion between them?

characters.name: Harry Bosch
characters.line: LAPD homicide detective; closed the Daisy Clayton case but lost Elizabeth to grief; suspects Edgar just committed murder.

characters.name: Jerry Edgar
characters.line: Bosch's partner; killed Jacques Avril in his home in a shooting Bosch believes was deliberate revenge, not self-defense.

characters.name: Chief Irving
characters.line: LAPD Chief; blackmailed out of the mayoral race after a 1996 cassette exposed his coverup of a former chief.

characters.name: Lt. Grace Billets
characters.line: Hollywood Division lieutenant; just navigated a fabricated sexual harassment complaint pushed by Captain Cooper.

characters.name: Madeline 'Maddie' Bosch
characters.line: Harry's daughter; briefly interned with Honey Chandler before resigning; dating Antonio.

characters.name: Honey Chandler
characters.line: Defense attorney who represented Alicia Kent's plea deal this season.

characters.name: Alicia Kent
characters.line: Physicist Stanley Kent's widow; convicted of conspiring with FBI agent Maxwell to murder her husband for his money.

characters.name: Agent Maxwell
characters.line: Rogue FBI agent and Alicia Kent's lover; killed during his arrest by his own partner Agent Reece.

characters.name: Elizabeth Clayton
characters.line: Recovering addict and Bosch's friend; overdosed after her daughter Daisy's killer accepted a bargained-down plea.

beats.label: S7 · Tamale Girl
beats.text: New Year's Eve arson kills apartment residents including a ten-year-old girl delivering tamales. Bosch investigates while Edgar spirals over the Avril shooting.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the arson case that drives the whole season and shows Edgar carrying S6's guilt.

beats.label: S7 · Franzen's Offer
beats.text: Chandler's fraudster client Vincent Franzen offers to expose bigger financier Carl Rogers to the SEC; Maddie assists Chandler in prepping him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the Rogers thread that will collide with Bosch's family.

beats.label: S7 · Chandler Shot
beats.text: Franzen and his girlfriend are murdered; Maddie finds Chandler bleeding out in her home. Rogers is confirmed as the ringleader behind the hit.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ties the two cases together and puts Maddie at the center of the season's threat.

beats.label: S7 · Judge Sobel
beats.text: Rogers's lawyer Fowkes hires a hitman who kills Fowkes, then Judge Sobel (Bosch's girlfriend), before dying in a shootout with Bosch and Robertson.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's most personal blow to Bosch and the end of the hitman thread.

beats.label: S7 · Billets Wins
beats.text: Billets exposes officers Leonard, Norris and Captain Cooper for harassment and corruption; all three are arrested. Chandler wakes from her coma.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resolves the Hollywood Division corruption arc and earns Billets her captaincy.

beats.label: S7 · Peña Released
beats.text: Bosch learns Peña was the true arsonist but Irving orders him released via a federal deal. Bosch defies orders and Irving suspends him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The core Bosch-vs-Irving conflict that severs their long alliance.

beats.label: S7 · Badge Turned In
beats.text: The tamale girl's father shoots Peña dead outside the station and is killed by police. Bosch turns in his badge; Maddie applies to the LAPD.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Bosch's exit from the LAPD is the launchpad for everything that follows.

cliffhanger.text: Bosch has surrendered his badge after the LAPD helped the true killer walk free. Peña is dead but by a father's hand, not the law's. Maddie is applying to become the very kind of officer her father just quit being.
questions: What does Bosch do next — private work, PI, or something else entirely?
Will Maddie actually join the LAPD, and how will Bosch feel watching her put on the badge?
Can Bosch's shattered trust in Irving and the department ever be repaired?

characters.name: Harry Bosch
characters.line: Just turned in his LAPD badge after being suspended for defying Irving's federal deal that freed the arson's true killer.

characters.name: Jerry Edgar
characters.line: Bosch's partner through the season; still shadowed by last year's Avril killing.

characters.name: Chief Irving
characters.line: LAPD Chief; ordered Peña's release and suspended Bosch, breaking their long alliance.

characters.name: Captain Grace Billets
characters.line: Just promoted to Captain after exposing officers Leonard, Norris and Captain Cooper for corruption and harassment.

characters.name: Madeline 'Maddie' Bosch
characters.line: Harry's daughter; witnessed Chandler's shooting and has just applied to the LAPD herself.

characters.name: Honey Chandler
characters.line: Defense attorney who woke from a coma after Rogers's hitman shot her; a long recovery ahead.

characters.name: Mickey Peña
characters.line: The true arsonist behind the tamale-girl fire; just shot dead outside the station by the girl's grieving father.
